| [THEORY-030](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-030.md) v2 | Landauer's principle prices only logically irreversible steps, and prices them in exported entropy rather than heat, so acquiring, copying or evaluating a bit, and learning it, carry no minimum thermodynamic cost | Bennett (2003), [LIT-360](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-360.md): the cost attaches to many-to-one maps of the logical state (erasure, merging of control flow), and it is at least k ln 2 of entropy exported per bit, which "need not" be heat. Information learnt is bounded by entropy production and can be paid almost entirely in weight entropy. The only per-bit heat term is Landauer's, on entropy removed. The synthesis across the three is the record's. It does not license a k_BT ln 2 heat floor per judgment, per gradient step or per bit learnt. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-039](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-039.md) | The later phases reported in neural-network training differ in kind: after the transition a network may simplify its weights, acquire item-specific information, lose generalisation, confine its tangent kernel or saturate its units, and none of these is a measured compression of I(X;T) | Nanda et al. | [THEORY-043](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-043.md) v4 | A mind of mindless agents and a mind of minded agents are one functionalist move run in two directions, and what separates them is an anti-nesting principle or an architectural criterion, neither yet principled | Minsky's society of mind builds a mind downward, out of agents that are not minds. Schwitzgebel ([LIT-159](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-159.md)) builds a candidate mind upward, out of agents that are. The readings agree that agency survives both directions: Block grants a homunculi-head beliefs, List grants organised groups agency and awareness, Levin finds nested goal-pursuing collectives (his "Selves") at every scale. The dispute narrows to phenomenal consciousness, and every published way to accept the downward move while refusing the upward one is either an anti-nesting principle (Putnam's stipulation, IIT's exclusion postulate, Kammerer's functional version), each introduced for or justified weakly by the verdict it gives, or an architectural criterion that would count against a loosely coupled society of mind as much as against a nation. Proposed: an account of where a dispute stands, from philosophical argument and no measurement. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-044](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-044.md) v2 | In relational frame theory the self is verbal behaviour's content, its process and its context, and the self as context is a perspective learned from deictic relations that cannot itself be found as content | Barnes-Holmes et al. ([LIT-541](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-541.md)) define three selves: the conceptualized self, the content of verbal relations about oneself; the knowing self, their ongoing process; and the transcendent self, their context. Hayes et al. ([LIT-555](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-555.md)) say the third arises from deictic frames (I–you, here–there, now–then) as "a sense of self as a locus or perspective", and is "a context for verbal knowing, not the content", so its limits "cannot be consciously known". The account maps the three onto the record's holdings: the content is the narrative self (Dennett, Gallagher, Strawson), and the context is what Hume could not find among his perceptions and what Metzinger calls a transparent perspective. It differs from the minimal self (Gallagher) on origin: RFT says the perspective is learned in language. The evidence for the learned origin is cited, not read, so Proposed. The clinical claim is [THEORY-051](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-051.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-045](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-045.md) | Felt affect is the experience of the body's regulatory state, valenced by what that state means for staying alive and present throughout waking experience, not only in emotion; whether what is felt is a prediction of that state or a map of it is unsettled | Barrett (2017), [LIT-542](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-542.md), and Damasio & Carvalho (2013), [LIT-388](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-388.md), are two independent accounts that agree on a base layer. What is felt as affect (valence and arousal for Barrett, feeling for Damasio) is the body's regulatory state. Its valence is that state's value for the organism, and it is present in hunger, pain and well-being as much as in emotion. They disagree about what the experience is of. For Barrett it is the brain's allostatic prediction of the body, issued from agranular limbic cortex. For Damasio it is a topographic map of the body's state, built in the upper brainstem, and their paper makes no use of prediction. Seth ([LIT-135](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-135.md)) builds on the same base but makes his claim about consciousness, not about affect. Friston ([LIT-526](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-526.md)) supports neither. Proposed: both sources are theoretical syntheses, and neither tests the claim. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-046](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-046.md) | Expected tangible rewards for merely engaging in an interesting task lower later free-choice engagement with it | Deci, Koestner and Ryan (1999, [LIT-557](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-557.md)): across 55 experiments, expected tangible rewards given for working on an interesting task lowered free-choice engagement after the reward stopped (d = −0.40; children −0.43, college students −0.21), and lowered self-reported interest less (−0.15). By their study-by-study account, Cameron and Pierce's rival analysis found the same for this contingency (performance-independent rewards, −0.29), while disputing nearly everything else. Proposed because the rival side is unread here. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-047](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-047.md) | A regulation taken in under controlling conditions is introjected rather than integrated, so the social history of how a value was acquired fixes how autonomous acting on it is | Deci and Ryan ([LIT-558](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-558.md)) and Ryan and Deci ([LIT-559](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-559.md)): supports for relatedness and competence are enough to get a value internalized, but only as an introject or a compartmentalized identification; integration also needs autonomy support. The experimental evidence is Deci et al. (1994), as reported: the same amount of internalized behaviour correlated positively with felt freedom and enjoyment under autonomy support and negatively under control. Field studies on parenting, religion and medical training agree, correlationally. This is a historical condition on autonomy of the kind [THEORY-040](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-040.md) asks about, with empirical support, but it has not been tested against matched present endorsement or applied to manipulation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-048](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-048.md) | In explaining psychiatric disorder, biological findings implement psychological functions rather than replacing them | Kendler (2008), [LIT-539](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-539.md): following Marr, a lower-level theory either replaces a higher-level construct (temperature by mean kinetic energy) or implements it, and in psychiatry biology "will implement but not replace psychology". The thesis is argued from neuroscience's successes in perception, learning and memory, not from a psychiatric case, so it is Proposed. It is a thesis about explanation, not about distinct mental causes: it survives Pernu's argument ([LIT-147](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-147.md)) that the neural evidence supports only mental causation by identity. Kendler 2005 ([LIT-552](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-552.md)), which argued the mind–brain propositions this paper develops, is unread. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-049](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-049.md) | Whether an external event lowers or raises intrinsic motivation depends on whether it is experienced as controlling or as information about competence | Cognitive evaluation theory, as tested by Deci, Koestner and Ryan (1999, [LIT-557](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-557.md)) and summarized by Ryan and Deci ([LIT-559](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-559.md)) and Deci and Ryan ([LIT-558](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-558.md)): rewards, feedback, deadlines and choice affect intrinsic motivation through their "functional significance". Controlling events shift the perceived locus of causality outward and undermine it; informational ones affirm competence and enhance it, but only with a sense of autonomy. The meta-analytic pattern fits, and controlling versus informational positive feedback differ by d = −0.78 in four studies. Mediation by felt control is untested for rewards. A behavioural and social-cognitive rival exists and is unread here. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-050](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-050.md) | Psychological inflexibility, in which verbal relations give private events aversive functions and make experiential avoidance a general strategy, is a transdiagnostic process in psychopathology | Hayes et al. ([LIT-555](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-555.md)) model psychopathology as inflexibility: cognitive fusion supports experiential avoidance, which narrows behaviour. Barnes-Holmes et al. ([LIT-541](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-541.md)) give the mechanism: once a word stands in derived relation to an event it can carry that event's aversive functions, so private events become worth avoiding. Kashdan and Rottenberg ([LIT-553](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-553.md)) find inflexibility across depression and anxiety in cognitive, behavioural and physiological systems, and say its causal role is unknown. The evidence is correlational, small, mostly self-report and mostly from the model's authors, and the meta-analysis that would test it ([LIT-543](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-543.md)) is unread, so Proposed. It is compatible with the loop account of disorder, not a rival to it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-051](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-051.md) v2 | Strengthening the self as context, a perspective from which thoughts about oneself are held as thoughts, is a process by which acceptance and commitment therapy reduces suffering | ACT names the self as context as one of its six processes: from it "one can be aware of ones own flow of experiences without attachment to them", so it fosters defusion and acceptance, and mindfulness exercises and metaphors foster it (Hayes et al., [LIT-555](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-555.md)). RFT reads defusion as moving thoughts from I HERE NOW to I THERE THEN, a deictic shift (Barnes-Holmes et al., [LIT-541](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-541.md)), labelled "no more than a heuristic". No study in the record tests the self as context as a process. Its only support is borrowed from small defusion studies under RFT's reading, so Proposed on weak grounds. The conceptual account of the self is [THEORY-044](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-044.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-052](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-052.md) | Frustration of the needs for autonomy, competence and relatedness is a transdiagnostic process in psychopathology | Vansteenkiste, Ryan and Soenens (2020, [LIT-561](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-561.md)) propose that need frustration, distinct from mere lack of satisfaction, plays "a transdiagnostic role", citing a longitudinal study in which it predicted adolescents' depressive and eating symptoms and "largely accounted for their co-occurrence". Deci and Ryan ([LIT-558](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-558.md)) had located the etiology of "various forms of psychopathology" in developmental need deprivation, with need substitutes, controlled styles and rigid patterns as the route. The evidence is correlational, mostly self-report, and from the theory's authors. A partner of the inflexibility account, not a rival. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-054](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-054.md) v2 | A regulation is autonomous to the degree it is integrated with one's other values and needs: autonomy is graded, and is not set by the order of the attitude that endorses it | Self-determination theory orders motives on a continuum from external through introjected and identified to integrated regulation and intrinsic motivation. Ryan and Deci ([LIT-559](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-559.md)) and Deci and Ryan ([LIT-558](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-558.md)) place autonomy in integration, "congruence with one's other values and needs", and report a quasi-simplex structure and an experiment in which integrated and introjected internalization behave differently. Ryan and Deci ([LIT-560](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-560.md)) align this with hierarchical accounts but grade it. It is the empirical counterpart of [THEORY-029](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-029.md)'s negative claim. It is not shown that integration can be measured apart from endorsement, and it does not escape Velleman's dilemma. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-055](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-055.md) | An appraisal of an event's pertinence to the agent's concerns elicits the emotion, as a state of action readiness, and emotions differ by their mode of action readiness | Frijda, Ridderinkhof & Rietveld (2014), [LIT-540](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-540.md), Frijda's own late statement of the theory of The Emotions ([LIT-546](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-546.md), unread). An automatic appraisal of how an event bears on one's concerns elicits a state of action readiness: a motive to change one's relation to the object, with control precedence. Emotions differ by mode (hostility for anger, avoidance for fear), and "in the absence of concern pertinence … no emotion". It is the record's only read statement of an appraisal theory, because Lazarus ([LIT-550](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-550.md)) is unread. Both the elicitation claim and the claim that emotions differ by mode are argued, and neither is tested. The second is partly definitional within the theory. Rivals [THEORY-057](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-057.md): both accounts let instances vary and group them by function, but the appraisal account puts the unity in the agent's readiness and the constructionist account puts it in the perceiver's concept. Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-056](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-056.md) v2 | Emotion regulation is not a process separate from emotion generation: most of it is one motive state checking another, with no distinct regulating system above them | Frijda, Ridderinkhof & Rietveld (2014), [LIT-540](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-540.md), deny "the exclusivity of emotion regulation processes". Appraising the consequences of an impulse raises a competing readiness, as when fear of retaliation holds back anger, so control is the interaction of motive states and not reason governing emotion. Barrett (2017), [LIT-542](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-542.md), reaches the second half from the opposite side of the emotion debate: automaticity and control are "different brain modes … not two battling brain systems", and she offers as a hypothesis that reappraisal works by the same predictions that construct emotion. Two rival theories of what an emotion is agree on this. Gross (1998), [LIT-554](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-554.md), poses the question and keeps the distinction. Proposed: argued from examples and from architecture, untested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-057](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-057.md) | Emotion categories are populations of variable instances grouped by the perceiver's concepts, not natural kinds with a shared neural or appraisal mechanism | Barrett (2017), [LIT-542](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-542.md): degeneracy, population thinking, and a table of findings in which no region, network, pattern or neuron is consistent for an emotion category. From these she concludes that categories such as fear are populations of variable instances, grouped by a goal and constructed by categorization with a concept. She rejects basic-emotion and causal appraisal theories as positing a "Lockean essence". This is the record's only read statement of the view. The record's philosophy holdings sharpen it. Pernu ([LIT-147](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-147.md)) shows that many-to-one realisation at a fine grain does not rule out one variable at a coarser grain, so degeneracy alone does not carry the conclusion, and Table 1 has to. Searle ([LIT-482](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-482.md)) shows that Barrett's comparison with money is to observer-relative function, not to institutions. Rivals the appraisal account, [THEORY-055](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-055.md). Proposed: one theoretical paper, no independent test, and the reply unread. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-058](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-058.md) v2 | Mental disorders are maintained by self-reinforcing causal loops rather than expressing a latent common cause, which is how they can outlast their triggers | Three traditions that do not cite one another for it put self-sustaining loops where a latent cause would be. Borsboom ([LIT-547](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-547.md)) makes disorder an alternative stable state of a strongly connected symptom network, kept up by hysteresis after its trigger has gone. Salkovskis, Sighvatsson and Sigurdsson ([LIT-538](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-538.md)) make it a threat meaning protected by the behaviour it drives. Kendler ([LIT-539](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-539.md)) finds causal loops across levels, from genes to culture. The convergence is real; the evidence is indirect, simulated or clinical, and none of it is an individual time series showing hysteresis, so the account is Proposed. It says nothing about what starts a disorder. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-059](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-059.md) | The readiness potential does not show that a neural decision to act precedes awareness of the urge to act | Libet read the readiness potential, which begins half a second or more before a spontaneous movement and before the reported urge, as the brain deciding first. Two independent arguments in the record remove that inference. Schurger, Sitt & Dehaene ([LIT-605](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-605.md)) show that a leaky accumulator driven by noise and fitted to waiting times alone reproduces the averaged readiness potential (r² = 0.96), because movement-locked averaging recovers the fluctuations that crossed threshold; a prediction of theirs held in 13 people. Dennett & Kinsbourne ([LIT-431](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-431.md)) argue that the clock report times a represented content, not an event in the brain. Proposed: the authors say their model shows the potential could be fluctuation, not that it is. It says nothing about whether the urge causes the act. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-060](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-060.md) | A life story constructed from adolescence on is the form a person's diachronic identity takes, and its content shapes later well-being | McAdams (2019), [LIT-595](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-595.md): narrative identity is "a person's internalized and evolving story of how he or she has become the person he or she is becoming", which gives a life "unity, moral purpose, and temporal coherence". It arrives in adolescence and young adulthood, on the back of autobiographical memory and autobiographical reasoning, as the third layer of a psychological self after the actor of traits and the agent of goals. Stories with agentic and redemptive themes go with well-being and generativity, and in one longitudinal therapy study the story "changes first, and then the storyteller gets better". A review essay: every finding is cited, not shown, and it concedes that having a life story may be a modern cultural construction. Strawson's "Against Narrativity" ([LIT-452](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-452.md)) denies the first half for many people. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-061](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-061.md) | In evidence-accumulation tasks, goals and instructions act on a decision by setting the parameters of the accumulation (drift, starting point or baseline, and threshold), not by specifying the response, and this holds for when to act as well as for which | Bogacz et al. ([LIT-569](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-569.md)) define cognitive control, in a two-choice task, as the adjustment of drift, starting point and threshold to maximise a utility. Ratcliff and McKoon ([LIT-576](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-576.md)) find that the manipulations behave that way: speed or accuracy instructions are fitted by boundary separation alone, stimulus proportions mainly by starting point, difficulty by drift alone. Schurger et al. ([LIT-605](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-605.md)) carry the picture to the decision of when to move: the task goal raises the baseline toward threshold and leaves the moment to fluctuation. The convergence is real; the evidence is group fits on a few paradigms, so Proposed. It does not say who sets the parameters, or how. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-062](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-062.md) | Model-based and model-free predictions both operate in instrumental and in Pavlovian learning, and which one controls behaviour follows their relative reliability, not the preference of a supervising system | Daw, Niv & Dayan ([LIT-580](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-580.md)) cast habitual and goal-directed instrumental control as model-free caching and model-based search, and let behaviour follow whichever estimate is less uncertain; simulations reproduce the effects of over-training, task complexity and reward proximity on devaluation. Dayan & Berridge ([LIT-584](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-584.md)) show from instant revaluation of a salt cue that Pavlovian prediction also has a model-based form, and suggest the same reliability arbitration there. Both controllers pursue the same ends; neither is the irrational one. The instrumental half is qualitative simulation; the Pavlovian half of the arbitration is a suggestion. Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-063](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-063.md) | The unity of experience is the integration of one global world-model into a single functional cluster, and it does not require a self-model | Metzinger's précis of Being No One (2005), [LIT-568](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-568.md): the globality constraint makes every conscious content part of one world-model. On the functional level that is "highest-order binding" into a single causal role, and on the neural level the prediction of "one single area of maximal causal density", after Tononi and Edelman's dynamic core. "What you subjectively experience upon experiencing your world as coherent is the high internal correlation strength between a subset of physical events in your own brain." A unified world comes before a self: the minimal case is "Selfless Snapshot Consciousness", and fully depersonalized states are "non-subjective consciousness". The neural half is a cited hypothesis, the précis says little is known, and how the cluster becomes one subject's is left open. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-064](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-064.md) | What is experienced as a self is the content of a self-model the system cannot recognise as a model, and nothing beyond such models is a self | Metzinger's précis of Being No One (2005), [LIT-568](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-568.md), with his encyclopedia article "Self models" ([LIT-450](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-450.md)): a phenomenal self is a transparent self-model, one whose representational character "is not accessible to subjective experience", so that the system experiences its content "simply as ourselves". Selfhood is "a function realized by a lack of information", and "no such things as selves exist in the world". Transparency is graded, and the perspective itself is modelled, as a phenomenal model of the intentionality relation. Two things are offered: a prediction (a wholly opaque self-model would abolish selfhood) and an ontological stipulation. The précis adds no evidence; its case studies are in the book, unread. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-065](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-065.md) | The unity that makes a movement an agent's action is achieved by conformity to the constitutive norms of agency, not given by the causal unity of a mind, so collective agents are agents in the same sense as individual ones | Korsgaard (2014), [LIT-587](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-587.md): an action is a movement "backed by the agent as a whole", and ordinary attribution implies that the agent was active and that the action expresses who she is. Following the categorical and hypothetical imperatives gives action the form of self-determined efficacy; the content of the maxims chosen under that form constitutes practical identity. Self-consciousness of one's own attitudes breaks the unity an animal is given, and reason is the work of rebuilding it, so unity of agency "is an achievement, not a given", and people can act together "in the most literal sense". The Tanner Lectures ([LIT-564](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-564.md)) supply the reflective structure the chapter assumes. Argued, with the Kantian premise assumed and the collective mechanism stated in a paragraph. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-067](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-067.md) | Self-control over time needs no faculty of will: interests that dominate at different delays bargain, and resolve is the recursive staking of expected future choices on the present one | Ainslie's précis ([LIT-586](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-586.md)): hyperbolic discounting makes a smaller, sooner reward temporarily preferred, so successive "interests" conflict as in a repeated prisoner's dilemma. Treating a choice as a precedent bundles the series, and summed hyperbolic curves favour the larger, later rewards; a lapse costs credibility. Will is that recursion, not an organ. Schelling ([LIT-602](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-602.md)) describes the same divided chooser from the side of tactics: we manage our later selves as we manage other people. The mathematics of bundling is sound; that willpower works this way is argued, and the précis concedes it is hard to test directly. It is a claim about how control is achieved, not about whose control is self-governance. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-069](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-069.md) | Rhythmic bimanual coordination switches from anti-phase to in-phase through a nonequilibrium phase transition in relative phase, captured by the HKB equation, with critical fluctuations and critical slowing as early warning | Kelso's 2021 retrospective ([LIT-601](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-601.md)) states the Haken–Kelso–Bunz model: relative phase φ between the hands obeys dφ/dt = −a sin φ − 2b sin 2φ, so in-phase and anti-phase are both stable for b/a > 1/4 and anti-phase loses stability below it as movement speeds up. With noise the switch is a nonequilibrium phase transition, and the reported data show enhanced fluctuations and critical slowing before it. Many effectors act as one through a collective variable, with no controller choosing the pattern. Proposed, because the 1985 paper and the 1986 stochastic analysis are unread and the data are held as their author reports them. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-070](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-070.md) | How much cognitive control to exert, and on what, is decided by a cost-benefit computation (the expected value of control) in a specification system distinct from the structures that implement the control | Shenhav, Botvinick & Cohen ([LIT-585](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-585.md)) unify dACC's many reported functions as one: deciding whether, where and how much control to allocate. A control signal has an identity (a task set, a threshold, an attention template) and an intensity; its expected value is its probability-weighted payoff, with future value discounted, minus an intrinsic cost rising with intensity. dACC monitors and specifies; lateral prefrontal and subcortical structures implement. The paper reviews evidence and fits nothing, so Proposed. It does not say what the cost is, how EVC is computed, or that it governs emotion regulation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-071](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-071.md) | Minimal agency requires individuality, interactional asymmetry and self-generated normativity, and individuality without the other two is not agency | Barandiaran, Di Paolo & Rohde (2009), [LIT-566](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-566.md), read in [NOTE-458](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-458.md). The three conditions are that the system distinguishes itself from its environment with no observer doing it, that it is the active source of modulations of its coupling with the environment, and that it regulates that coupling against norms its own organisation sets. Each is necessary, and together they are claimed to be sufficient. Individuality is the precondition of the other two and does not suffice. A cell in passive osmosis, a kitten warmed by its mother and a person with a Parkinsonian tremor are each individuals, and none of them is acting. The generative definition is an open autonomous organisation that adaptively modulates its coupling so as to maintain itself. Here "autonomy" and "self" mean organisational closure. They do not mean a subject or self-governance. Proposed: a conceptual analysis checked against intuitive cases, with an asymmetry criterion its authors call incomplete. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-072](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-072.md) | Organisms differ from dissipative structures such as a candle flame not by far-from-equilibrium self-maintenance, nor by circular self-maintenance alone, but by organisational differentiation: several distinct constraints that produce one another at different time scales | The record's first answer to the demarcation question that [NOTE-094](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-094.md) reports. Prigogine ([LIT-516](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-516.md)) supplies the dissipative structures, and nothing in his account separates them from organisms. Mossio, Saborido & Moreno (2009, [LIT-570](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-570.md)) grant a candle flame organisational closure. Its one macroscopic pattern keeps up the conditions of the combustion that makes it. They draw the line at organisational differentiation: in an organism several distinct structures make distinct contributions, where a flame makes "a unique contribution". Montévil & Mossio (2015, [LIT-582](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-582.md)) narrow closure to mutual dependence among constraints. Each constraint must be both produced by and productive of another, with at least one slow and one fast dependence. On the record's reading, that builds differentiation into closure. No paper analyses a flame under the 2015 definitions. Neither paper says closure defines an organism. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-073](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-073.md) | A Markov blanket does not individuate a system: where it falls is fixed by modelling choices made before it is found, so it presupposes the boundary it is used to find, and it cannot represent a boundary the system produces | Bruineberg et al. ([LIT-603](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-603.md)) and Raja et al. ([LIT-598](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-598.md)) argue, by different routes, that the Markov blanket of the free-energy literature is placed and not found. The formal core is [THEORY-066](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-066.md): the partition takes the internal set as input. This account adds what the critiques show about practice. In Friston's soup ([LIT-526](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-526.md)) the graph was built from one kind of coupling and steady state was assumed when the run stopped. In published applications the blanket sits wherever the model needs it: in the receptors of a brain, the membrane of a bacillus, the beam joining two pendulums. The formalism also gives the same description to a membrane the cell makes and a beam nobody's states make. So the blanket presupposes the boundary it is offered as the criterion of. Proposed: the argument is conceptual, and the later steady-state definitions have not been read. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-074](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-074.md) | Implicit accessibility of the true self-concept is not what self-report scales of authenticity or of need satisfaction measure, though those two self-reports are not shown to be separate constructs | Schlegel, Hicks, Arndt & King (2009), [LIT-606](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-606.md): true-self accessibility, the speed of "me" judgments for traits a person takes to be her true self, correlated .05 with AI-3 authenticity and .20 with basic need satisfaction (N = 124), and each predicted meaning in life independently. The authors read this as showing the constructs differ, and concede the difference is confounded with method, reaction time against self-report. The two self-reports correlated .52, and felt autonomy was only one third of the need-satisfaction composite, whose autonomy items include "I can pretty much be myself". So the paper separates the implicit measure from both self-reports, and does not separate authenticity from autonomy. Proposed: one sample for the correlations, method unresolved. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-075](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-075.md) | Obligation is the reflective rejection of what would violate the agent's practical identity, and moral obligation follows only because valuing any practical identity commits the agent to valuing her humanity | Korsgaard (1992), [LIT-564](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-564.md): because human consciousness is reflective, an agent must act on reasons, and so must identify with some law, a "practical identity": "a description under which you value yourself". "Your reasons express your identity, your nature; your obligations spring from what that identity forbids." Obligation is "the reflective rejection of a threat to your identity", unconditional where violation would be worse than death. Identities are a "jumble" and differ across social worlds, so this much yields no morality. Moral obligation enters because valuing any identity requires valuing one's humanity, the source of all one's reasons. "The Normative Constitution of Agency" ([LIT-587](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-587.md)) later makes practical identity the content of maxims chosen under the formal norms. Argued, with the key steps flagged by their author as sketchy; the commentaries and reply are unread. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-076](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-076.md) | Diachronic self-governance is constituted by cross-temporal links of intention that are intrapersonal analogues of shared intention, not by narrative unity and not by intertemporal bargaining | Bratman (2018), [LIT-567](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-567.md): an agent governs herself over time when she is self-governing at each time along a planned activity and her intentions at those times interlock as the intentions of people acting together do, so that she acts "together" with herself. Her standpoints include a conditional, reflexive end of her own diachronic self-governance, which is what lets resolve against temptation be self-governed while following through on Kavka's toxin is not. He rejects the bargaining model (McClennen, Ainslie) in two sentences and calls narrative unity less basic in one. A philosophical model argued from cases; the analogy is partial by its author's account and its terms come from a book the record has not read. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-077](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-077.md) | Goals pursued for identified or intrinsic reasons receive more sustained effort, which carries their better attainment, and attaining them raises well-being more than attaining goals pursued under pressure | Sheldon & Elliot (1999), [LIT-589](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-589.md): a goal is self-concordant to the degree its reasons are identified or intrinsic rather than external or introjected. In two semester-long student samples, self-concordance predicted sustained effort, and effort fully carried its link to attainment (self-concordance β = .02 and .08, ns, with effort in the model). In the same two samples attainment raised well-being more when goals were self-concordant (interaction β = .11, .23), partly through accumulated daily experiences of autonomy, competence and relatedness. Everything is self-report and correlational, and the structural models fit only after revision. It is evidence for the autonomous end of SDT's continuum, not for integration as distinct from identification. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-078](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-078.md) | The top C eigenvalues of a trained C-class classifier's Fisher are carried by the second moment of its class-mean logit derivatives, so a cut at the bulk edge keeps the span of the class means, and they stand clear of the bulk to the extent between-class separation exceeds within-class variation | Papyan (2019), [LIT-619](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-619.md): for softmax cross-entropy the Gauss–Newton matrix G, which is the model's Fisher averaged over inputs, is an uncentred second moment of logit derivatives indexed by class and logit. It decomposes exactly into four terms (Eq. 28), and its top C eigenvalues match those of the class-mean term G₁. Papyan (2020), [LIT-613](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-613.md), splits those C into one global-mean outlier and C − 1 between-class ones, finds a C(C − 1) cross-class mini-bulk beneath them, and proves the whole pattern for a Gaussian toy model. Papyan (2018), [LIT-617](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-617.md), supplies the measurements and the attribution of the Hessian's outliers to G. The decomposition is algebra. That G₁ carries the outliers is measured, by eye, under a training protocol narrower than practice. So this is Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-079](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-079.md) | Bayesian model reduction under the Laplace approximation prices the reductions of a singular parent model with a Gaussian Occam factor, so its free-energy differences can be wrong by a term that grows with log n | The filer's synthesis, stated by no source. BMR's closed form (Friston & Penny, [LIT-620](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-620.md), Eq. 9; Friston, Parr & Zeidman, [LIT-614](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-614.md), Eq. 11) charges a reduction through log-determinants of Gaussian precisions, which is MacKay's regular Occam factor. Watanabe, [LIT-616](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-616.md), says that models with hierarchical layers or hidden variables are singular, that no normal distribution approximates their posterior, and that their free energy grows as λ log n. BMR is applied to exactly such models: mixtures, hierarchical empirical Bayes and latent states. Neither literature cites the other. The exact identity is untouched ([THEORY-081](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-081.md)). The claim is about its Laplace form, and a test on reduced-rank regression would settle it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-080](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-080.md) | In a linearised network with a Gaussian prior on its parameters, the Occam factor is a sum over the NTK's eigenvalues, so on spherical data each harmonic pays ½ log(1 + βnµ_k/α) and the kernel's eigenvalue decay schedules the complexity penalty across frequencies | The filer's synthesis, stated by no source. A network linearised at initialisation, with an isotropic Gaussian prior on its parameters and Gaussian noise, is MacKay's linear-in-parameters model ([LIT-623](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-623.md)). Its Occam factor is −½ Σ log(1 + βλ_a/α) over the eigenvalues of JᵀJ. These are the empirical NTK's, which on uniform spherical data form Bietti & Bach's degree blocks, nµ_k with multiplicity N(d, k) ([LIT-608](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-608.md)). Degrees whose βnµ_k exceeds α pay about ½ log n per harmonic, and degrees below pay almost nothing. With µ_k ~ k^(−d), the number of paid directions γ grows as n^((d−1)/d), not as the parameter count. Basri et al.'s bound ([LIT-612](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-612.md), Eq. 14) is the matching data-fit term. The kernel's decay exponent is the schedule of the penalty. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-083](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-083.md) | Training a classifier past zero training error collapses its last-layer features onto their class means and drives the centred means toward a simplex equiangular tight frame, with the classifier aligned to them and the decision becoming nearest class mean | Papyan, Han & Donoho (2020), [LIT-618](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-618.md), measured 480 trained classifiers on seven datasets with VGG, ResNet and DenseNet. Through the terminal phase, within-class variability of last-layer features falls (NC1), and the centred class means become equinorm and equiangular with cosine −1/(C − 1) (NC2). The classifier aligns with them (NC3), and the decision becomes nearest class mean (NC4). They prove that NC1 and NC2 imply NC3 and NC4 for the MSE-optimal and max-margin classifiers, and that the simplex ETF is the unique error-exponent-optimal codebook. Papyan (2020), [LIT-613](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-613.md), sees class means separate and grow more orthogonal with depth. The measurements cover one protocol, and the dynamics are unexplained. The paper's further claim, that the Hessian's class outliers are a symptom of collapse, is argued and not measured, and is left to [THEORY-078](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-078.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-084](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-084.md) | Because the Gauss–Newton Fisher JᵀJ and the NTK Gram matrix JJᵀ share their non-zero spectrum, the lazy-regime Fisher of a ReLU network on spherical data inherits the NTK's harmonic-degree blocks, and a spectral threshold on it is well posed only at gaps between blocks | The filer's synthesis, stated by no source. The identity is linear algebra: JᵀJ (parameters × parameters) and JJᵀ (samples × samples) have the same non-zero eigenvalues. Under squared loss JᵀJ is the Gauss–Newton matrix and the Fisher. JJᵀ is the empirical NTK Gram matrix, which in the kernel regime on uniform spherical data has the degree-block spectrum of Bietti & Bach (2021), [LIT-608](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-608.md): µ_k with multiplicity N(d, k). The threshold claim draws on Cao et al. (2019), [LIT-624](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-624.md). Their guarantees are stated only for whole eigenspaces, with sample costs that grow as the gap below them shrinks. It also draws on Basri et al. (2019), [LIT-612](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-612.md), where a structural zero block shows up in a finite sample as small non-zero eigenvalues. No paper filed computes a Fisher spectrum in this regime. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-085](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-085.md) | A classifier's class-driven Fisher outliers pair each class's feature mean with that class's own error mean, so K-FAC's single Kronecker product of class-averaged factors adds every cross-class pairing and misplaces them, and differs from the class-wise product by the between-class covariance of its two factors | Papyan (2020), [LIT-613](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-613.md): per layer, the Fisher is a weighted sum of Kronecker products of features and backpropagated errors (Eq. 7.5), and its class outliers come from class means of gradients that are approximately h_c ⊗ δ_c. K-FAC (Martens & Grosse 2015, [LIT-622](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-622.md)) multiplies the class-averaged feature covariance by the class-averaged error covariance. Papyan finds its outliers and mini-bulks "drastically misaligned", and the class-wise CFAC aligns much better at deep layers. The filer adds a line of algebra: CFAC − K-FAC = Ave_c (H_c − H̄) ⊗ (Δ_c − Δ̄), so the two coincide when one factor's per-class statistics do not vary with class. The evidence is one MLP, spectra only, judged by eye. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-087](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-087.md) | The Bayesian complexity penalty grows as (d/2) log n in a regular model, where the curvature at the optimum sets the Occam factor, and as λ log n in a singular one, where λ is the real log canonical threshold and falls below d/2 when the prior is positive on the optimal set | MacKay (1992), [LIT-623](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-623.md), writes the evidence as best-fit likelihood times an Occam factor, the ratio of posterior to prior accessible volume, which under a Gaussian approximation is P(w_MP)(2π)^{k/2} det^{-1/2}A. When the likelihood dominates, det A grows as n^d, so the penalty is (d/2) log n. Watanabe's WBIC paper, [LIT-616](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-616.md), recovers that case (Lemma 3, Theorem 5) and states what replaces it when the Fisher information is degenerate at the optimum: λ log n − (m − 1) log log n, with λ the RLCT (Theorem 2). The regular half is derived. The singular half is a theorem the record holds only as cited, so this is Proposed. The volume reading of λ is in Watanabe's book, which is unread. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-088](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-088.md) | Slow large-scale activity in human cortex is organised as in a pattern-forming medium: its flow is set by interacting spiral defects centred on phase singularities, which sit on boundaries between functional regions, annihilate with spirals of opposite rotation and repel those of the same | Xu, Long, Feng & Gong (2023), [LIT-638](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-638.md): in Human Connectome Project fMRI band-passed to 0.01–0.1 Hz, the cortical phase field holds about 16–19 spirals at a time around phase singularities, concentrated on boundaries between functional regions; their centres drift superdiffusively, opposite spirals annihilate (51% fully, 46% partly) and like ones repel (2.6%), and their positions and senses decode task condition above a raw-amplitude decoder. One source, fMRI only, at a spatial scale chosen because it maximised that decoding; the routing of activity flow is read from phase gradients and a phase-oscillator model, never perturbed. The kinship with Belousov–Zhabotinsky spirals and pattern-formation defects is the record's analogy, not the paper's. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-089](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-089.md) | The content of a mental representation has two factors, a narrow conceptual role inside the head and a referential factor relating it to the world, and a long-arm role theory that gets Twin Earth truth conditions right reduces to the same two | Block (1986), [LIT-648](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-648.md), and Block (1987), [LIT-625](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-625.md). Meaning has a conceptual-role component "entirely 'in the head'", an expression's "total causal role, abstractly described" in inference and decision, which twins share and which explains their behaviour, and an external component relating representations to referents and truth conditions. Conceptual role fixes the nature of the referential factor, not reference. A one-factor theory with long-arm roles must, to get Twin Earth truth conditions right, import normal context, causal chains of borrowed reference and experts; chop off what lies outside the skin and the rest is the short-arm role, so the difference is "merely verbal". Social meaning is assigned to the referential factor or to a third, social factor, and is only sketched. Proposed: no identity conditions for roles, and narrow content is given room, not shown explanatory. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-090](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-090.md) | A basic, affective form of consciousness is realised subcortically, in the upper brainstem and thalamus, before and without cortex, and its first function is alarm: survival behaviour, care for the body and generalised one-shot learning, with no choice between options | Newen & Montemayor's ALARM theory (2025), [LIT-626](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-626.md): basic arousal, a sensitivity to pain, pleasure and other basic affect without focused attention, can be realised without cortex, by the upper brainstem and thalamus, and its function is to alarm the bodily agent when a homeostatic variable leaves its range, giving the signal "100% weight" through "rather rigid behavioural programmes without choices". Damasio & Carvalho (2013), [LIT-388](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-388.md), supply the subcortical clause independently: feeling is generated in the upper brainstem and the insula is not needed. Both papers argue from cited evidence and offer no new data, and neither has a marker that tells a felt alarm from an unfelt one. The function clause rests on ALARM alone, and Veit's account rivals it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-091](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-091.md) | A deficit in which consciousness and a capacity are lost together does not show that the capacity is a function of phenomenal consciousness, since access is lost too and the capacity is one the machinery of access has | Block (1995), [LIT-643](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-643.md), §6. Marcel, Flanagan, van Gulick and Schacter argue from the thirsty blindsight patient who does not reach for the water, and Searle from Penfield's petit mal automatisms, that a function of phenomenal consciousness is to let information guide action. In blindsight access is missing too, and in petit mal nothing shows experience is missing at all. "The fallacy is: an obvious function of the machinery of access-consciousness is illicitly transferred to phenomenal consciousness." That experience causes access, so that the function is experience's after all, is "a bold hypothesis, not a fallacy", and the deficit cannot decide it. Proposed: single-source, and the distinction it rests on is argued from conceivable cases. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-092](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-092.md) | Behavioural capacity does not fix intelligence: a system with the capacity to respond sensibly to every possible input can lack it, so whether behaviour is intelligent, or the mark of any mental property, depends partly on how it is produced | Block (1981), [LIT-642](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-642.md): the strongest behaviourist conception of intelligence, a capacity to give sensible responses to any sequence of inputs, "whatever they may be", is met by a machine that stores every sensible conversation of a test's length and looks up its next reply, yet "the machine has the intelligence of a toaster". So psychologism is true: two systems alike in all actual and counterfactual behaviour can differ in intelligence through the processing that mediates it. Block (1995), [LIT-630](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-630.md), n. 1: the same machine refutes the wider claim that there is no mental difference without a behavioural one. It is a claim about constitution, not evidence: performance stays evidence for competence. It names no required kind of processing, and its machine is a lookup table, not a trained network. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-093](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-093.md) | A content of mind is conscious when a continuous flow of homeostatic feelings identifies it as the organism's own; the feelings are conscious in themselves and hybrid, partly made of the body state they map, because interoceptive pathways let the body act directly on the neurons that map it | Damasio & Damasio (2022), [LIT-628](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-628.md), an essay with no data, read only through a summarising fetch tool, so its wording is paraphrased here. Consciousness is the spontaneous identification of mind contents as belonging to one's own organism, and a continuous stream of homeostatic feelings, from hunger and pain to a faint feeling of existing, supplies it; the feelings are conscious in themselves and confer consciousness on exteroceptive images. They are hybrid because interoceptive axons are unmyelinated, partly non-synaptic and outside a systematic blood–brain barrier, so viscera and circulating molecules act on the neurons that map them. Damasio & Carvalho (2013), [LIT-388](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-388.md), read in full, supply the upper-brainstem site of feeling and the unmyelinated-fibre proposal. Proposed: the identification is a definition, the mechanism an interpretation of anatomy, and the clinical evidence does not separate this account from its rivals. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-094](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-094.md) | Neither report nor no-report paradigms isolate the neural basis of consciousness, because post-perceptual cognition that tracks the percept persists without report; only a design that removes differential post-perceptual cognition does | Block (2007), [LIT-646](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-646.md), framed the methodological puzzle: the neural basis of experience can be found only by deciding whether it includes the machinery of access, and the evidence comes through report. The no-report paradigm was the answer. Block (2019), [LIT-637](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-637.md), argues it has "a fatal flaw": subjects not asked to report still think about what they see, and that thought is aligned with the percept (the "bored monkey" problem). Eliminating report isolates the basis of experience "only if it eliminates post-perceptual cognitive processing" correlated with the percept. Brascamp et al.'s inconspicuous rivalry, whose switches subjects detected at chance, is the one such design Block offers. The method is specific to rivalry so far, and Block says there may be no general solution. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-095](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-095.md) | Phenomenal character is not fixed by long-arm functional role or by externally individuated representational content: on Inverted Earth it stays the same while both invert, so only internal accounts, short-arm functional or physical, remain open | Block (1990), [LIT-634](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-634.md): on Inverted Earth colours and colour words are inverted, so a subject fitted with inverting lenses notices nothing. After long residence, or for a twin with a molecule-for-molecule identical brain raised there, the intentional content of the experience of the sky inverts and so does its long-arm functional role, while qualitative content stays the same; Q = F₁, Q = F₂ and F₁ ≠ F₂ breaks transitivity of identity. Block (2003), [LIT-635](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-635.md), turns the case on externalist representationism: for colour there is no shared appearance property left to explain the sameness, and long-term memory blocks the gradual-shift reply, so "mental paint" is what stays the same. Proposed: both rest on an externalist shift of content and on first-person sameness, and Block concedes that a short-arm functional theory of qualia would escape. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-096](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-096.md) | Perceptual consciousness is global availability: a content becomes conscious when the activity it drives into a core of long-range hub neurons, prefrontal among them, crosses a threshold and ignites it, so that the network amplifies, sustains and broadcasts that one content to the specialised processors; below threshold it leaves a decaying wave and is not experienced | Mashour, Roelfsema, Changeux & Dehaene (2020), [LIT-631](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-631.md), a review by the theory's proponents. Conscious access is "a non-linear network ignition" that amplifies and sustains a representation so that local processors can access it, in a distributed core of long-range layer II/III and V pyramidal neurons with prefrontal cortex a key hub but "not ... the exclusive territory". Ignition is exclusive: one content at a time. Evidence: seen and unseen trials diverge after about 200 ms across modalities; in van Vugt et al.'s monkeys, missed stimuli drove V1 and V4 but only reported ones, and false alarms, ignited sustained prefrontal firing, and the signal-detection threshold is the ignition threshold. The review adopts the premise that global availability "is what we subjectively experience as a conscious state", and calls experience without access untested; that premise, not the access data, is where it rivals overflow and the sensory account. Single source, second-hand evidence, and the P3 question conceded open. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-097](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-097.md) | Long-range coordination in the human forebrain is carried by brief ripples that co-occur at distant sites: during them neurons co-fire more whatever the distance between them, and at retrieval they carry stimulus-specific reinstatement of encoding co-firing | Verzhbinsky, Daume, Cheng, Rutishauser & Halgren (2026), [LIT-633](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-633.md): in 1,373 single units from five bilateral forebrain regions of 35 epilepsy patients doing a Sternberg task, ripples (70–100 Hz, about 70 ms) co-occur between bundles at a median 5% at every tract distance from 71 to 223 mm, and unit pairs co-fire a median 34% more during co-ripples than in no-ripple periods, beyond a rate-only null and with no loss over distance. The gain rises with load (13% in maintenance, 19% at retrieval), and encoding co-firing for a stimulus recurs at retrieval in 0.29% of cell-pair trials in co-ripples against 0.14% outside them. Correlational throughout: one task, two load levels, clinically placed electrodes, nothing perturbed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-098](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-098.md) | The neural basis of perceptual consciousness does not include the prefrontal machinery of cognitive access: it is recurrent activity in sensory cortex | Block's "back of the head" position, from three papers. Block (2005), [LIT-629](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-629.md): a phenomenal NCC (for seen motion, recurrent MT/V5–V1 activity) and an access NCC (frontoparietal broadcasting), with winner-take-all access letting a recurrent sensory representation lose and stay unaccessed. Block (2007), [LIT-646](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-646.md): the mesh argument. If workspace activation is not part of the basis of experience, strong losing sensory coalitions explain why experience overflows access; if it is, nothing does. Block (2019), [LIT-637](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-637.md): no-report designs do not settle the prefrontal question, because thought about the percept persists, and one design that removes it found no prefrontal difference by fMRI, which Block calls evidence against prefrontalism while granting that ECoG could still support it. Proposed: an inference to the best explanation, with every experiment second-hand and the decisive test not yet run. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-099](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-099.md) | Tryptophan networks in microtubule architectures support collective superradiant excitonic states, and their thermal quantum yield rises with network size and survives static disorder of room-temperature size | Babcock et al. (2024), [LIT-645](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-645.md): a radiative Hamiltonian of up to more than 10⁵ tryptophan transition dipoles, on tubulin geometry, predicts superradiant states up to about 4000 times the single-tryptophan rate in a centriole, and a thermal quantum yield that rises with network size and is almost unaffected by static disorder of about 200 cm⁻¹, though that disorder cuts the brightest state's enhancement from about 3600 to about 20. Steady-state spectroscopy finds a tryptophan quantum yield of 17.6 ± 2.1% in microtubules against 10.6 ± 0.6% in tubulin dimers. No lifetimes were measured. This is not evidence for Orch OR or for any claim about consciousness. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-100](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-100.md) | A neural correlate of conscious report does not require laminar cortex: in crows it is carried by the nidopallium caudolaterale, a nuclear pallial region whose neurons follow the reported percept rather than the stimulus | Maldarelli & Güntürkün (2025), [LIT-650](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-650.md), reviewing Nieder et al. (2020): in crows reporting near-threshold stimuli, single neurons in the nidopallium caudolaterale (NCL), the functional analogue of prefrontal cortex, fired with the "seen" report whether or not a stimulus was shown and were silent on "not seen" reports. NCL is nuclear, not layered; the cortex-like layers and columns found in birds are confined to the sensory pallium. So a correlate of conscious report does not need laminar cortex. The crow evidence is second-hand, from one laboratory and not in the record, and a report paradigm cannot separate access from phenomenal consciousness. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-101](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-101.md) | Consciousness began as hedonic valence, which evolved as a common currency for trading off competing options in action selection among animals with many degrees of freedom | Veit's pathological complexity thesis, as he restates and defends it in his reply to commentators (2025), [LIT-105](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-105.md): consciousness originated as hedonic valence, "a common currency of sharing evaluative information across multiple control systems", which animals with many degrees of freedom need to solve the combinatorial trade-offs of action selection. Felt valence is identical with that currency, "not Cartesian but cybernetic". Motivational trade-offs are his criterion for consciousness. The source is a reply piece; the thesis is argued in a book the record has not read, and the mechanism is a sketch. ALARM ([THEORY-090](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-090.md)) rivals it on what the first consciousness did. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-102](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-102.md) | In human ventral temporal cortex the content of a clearly seen, unchanging image is carried for as long as it stays on by a stable population code while activity amplitude decays; prefrontal and parietal content is a transient event at onset | Vishne, Gerber, Knight & Deouell (2023), [LIT-644](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-644.md): in 430 visually responsive subdural electrodes from 10 patients viewing images for 300–1,500 ms with no report on analysed trials, high-frequency activity and single-electrode category selectivity fell about 80% from peak by 800–900 ms, while the pattern across ventral temporal electrodes kept near-ceiling, time-invariant category and exemplar information that ended a fixed delay after the image went off. Prefrontal and parietal information was confined to about 150–600 ms and ignored duration. This met the predictions both IIT's and the global workspace's proponents registered for the paradigm, so it did not discriminate them. Above- threshold images only, sparse right-lateralised frontal coverage, one frequency band; it does not show the code tracks experience rather than input. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-103](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-103.md) | Perceptual consciousness overflows cognitive access: in partial-report tasks more items are experienced than the roughly four that working memory holds, though any one of them can be accessed when cued | Block (2007), [LIT-646](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-646.md), and Block (2011), [LIT-640](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-640.md). Subjects shown 8–32 items say they see all or almost all of them, report about 4, and when cued after offset can report or compare most of any cued subset: capacity 6–7 of 8 up to 1.5 s (Landman et al.), and 7, 6 and 5 of 8 at 1, 2.5 and 4 s (fragile visual short-term memory), against a working memory that stays at about 4. Block reads the surplus as experienced. The rival "sparse" reading holds it in an unconscious store plus a conscious generic or fragmentary image, and Block argues there is no independent evidence for either posit. Proposed: every experiment is second-hand, and that the surplus is conscious is the contested step. Overflow means most items are unaccessed, not that any is inaccessible. | Proposed |
